I have a complete picture. Here is my report.

## Summary of findings

Note up front: there is a clear mismatch between the current implementation and what the acceptance test expects. The test file describes an "identity-key-v2" (SHA-256 hex over `normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName)`), but the shipped `Owner.getIdentityKey()` returns a plaintext `telephone|email|householdId` string. The `Soundex` class exists but is not referenced by any production code, and `HouseholdDuplicateException` is defined but never thrown. Details below.

---

### 1. Where identityKey is computed

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (lines 287-300):

```java
public String getIdentityKey() {
    return (this.telephone == null ? "" : this.telephone) + '|'
        + (this.email == null ? "" : this.email) + '|'
        + (this.householdId == null ? "" : this.householdId);
}
```

This is the actual key used for duplicate detection: normalized telephone `|` email `|` householdId, as plaintext. It does NOT use SHA-256, soundex, or lastName. Supporting hash/soundex utilities:
- SHA-256 helper: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/util/Sha256Hex.java` (`upperHexPrefix` line 41, `lowerHex` line 53).
- Soundex: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/util/Soundex.java` (`encode` line 50). Defined but unused anywhere in `src/main` (only referenced in the test's comment).

The identityKey is surfaced to clients via MapStruct auto-mapping (Owner has `getIdentityKey()`, OwnerDto has the field per `openapi.yml` line 2240). The OpenAPI contract at `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` lines 2240-2250 describes it as the plaintext `telephone||household` form (example `'+61412345678||'`) — matching the implementation, not the test.

### 2. Duplicate detection returning 409 Conflict

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

`rejectWhenIdentityInUse` (lines 380-388):
```java
private void rejectWhenIdentityInUse(Owner owner) {
    String identityKey = owner.getIdentityKey();
    boolean inUse = existingOwners()
        .anyMatch(existing -> identityKey.equals(existing.getIdentityKey()));
    if (inUse) {
        throw new DuplicateIdentityException(
            "An owner with identity key " + identityKey + " already exists");
    }
}
```
Called from the create pipeline `createOwner` at line 229. The pipeline order is in `createOwner` (lines 214-252).

The exception -> 409 mapping:
- `DuplicateIdentityException` extends `OwnerConflictException` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/DuplicateIdentityException.java`).
- Handled in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java` `handleOwnerConflictException` (lines 138-142), which maps every `OwnerConflictException` to `HttpStatus.CONFLICT`.
- Base classes: `OwnerConflictException` and `OwnerRuleException` in the same `advice` package.

### 3. Soft-match logic (soundex + postcode)

The shipped soft match uses lastName + postcode + differing telephone — NOT soundex. In `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

`assignPossibleDuplicate` (lines 406-414) and `isPossibleDuplicateOf` (lines 426-433):
```java
private boolean isPossibleDuplicateOf(Owner existing, Owner owner) {
    return existing.getPostcode() != null
        && existing.getPostcode().equals(owner.getPostcode())
        && existing.getLastName() != null
        && existing.getLastName().equalsIgnoreCase(owner.getLastName())
        && existing.getTelephone() != null
        && !existing.getTelephone().equals(owner.getTelephone());
}
```
This sets the `possibleDuplicate` / `possibleDuplicateOf` flags on the Owner (fields in `Owner.java` lines 93-97). Soundex is NOT used here; matching is exact case-insensitive lastName + exact postcode. The `Soundex` util (item 1) is the only soundex code and it is unreferenced.

### 4. householdId computation and household-duplicate 409

- Computation: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/util/HouseholdNormalizer.java`, `householdId` (lines 54-56):
```java
public String householdId(String lastName, String postcode) {
    return Sha256Hex.upperHexPrefix(normalizeLastName(lastName) + '|' + (postcode == null ? "" : postcode), 12);
}
```

          title: Address line 1

            collapsed, upper-cased and common street-type abbreviations expanded).

          maxLength: 255

          title: Address line 2

            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. It is then stored and returned in that E.164 form (e.g.
            '0412 345 678' becomes '+61412345678'). A value that cannot form

            household id) so it is never flagged as a possible duplicate. Owners

                separated by a single space (e.g. 'DR Franklin') when a title is
                present, or just the last name when no title is given. Derived on
                read from the stored title and last name.

              example: 'DR Franklin'

              title: Telephone display
              description: >-

                threes. Derived on read from the stored 'telephone', which stays
                raw E.164.
              type: string

                SHA-256 digest over the normalized telephone concatenated with the
                last name. Carries no sequence number.

              maximum: 9

              title: Household ID

                household (same last name and postcode), computed as the first
                12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the normalized last name and
                the postcode joined with '|'. Every owner with the same last name
                and postcode carries the same value automatically; it is always
                assigned.

                normalized telephone, the lower-cased email (or empty when
                absent) and the household id (or empty when absent) joined with
                '|'. A new owner is rejected with 409 Conflict only when its
                whole identity key equals an existing owner's.

            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number

                (business-day-adjusted) registration date (e.g. 'NSW-A1B2C3D4-M26').

            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner, one of MR, MRS, MS or
            DR. When present it is combined with the last name to form the
            owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string
          enum:
            - MR
            - MRS
            - MS
            - DR
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1' is supplied it is
            preferred and the returned 'address' is composed from the normalized
            structured lines. On read it is the composed, normalized address: the
            normalized 'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized
            'addressLine2' appended when an 'addressLine2' is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Optional;
            when a non-blank value is supplied it is preferred over the flat
            'address' input. Stored and returned normalized (trimmed, whitespace
            collapsed, upper-cased and common street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '10 King Street'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address.
            When present it is stored and returned normalized and appended to the
            composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: 'Apartment 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. It is then stored and returned in that E.164 form (e.g.
            '0412 345 678' becomes '+61412345678'). A value that cannot form
            valid E.164 is rejected with 400.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must
            be valid for the owner's city per the fixed region ranges
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099 for cities in the
            Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD table); a city with no
            known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. A malformed or
            out-of-range postcode is rejected with 400. It is stored and
            returned unchanged.
          type: string
          minLength: 4
          maxLength: 4
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create the server sets it to its current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is used to derive the owner's 'ageBand'
            (computed against the registration date).
          type: string
          format: date

                stored first and last names.

              description: >-

                first and last names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true

                REGION is the region derived from the postcode (falling back to the
                city) and HASH8 is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the
                SHA-256 digest over the normalized telephone concatenated with the
                last name. Carries no sequence number.

## Summary

I redesigned the identity key and duplicate detection to match the new specification. All tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 2/2).

### Changes

**`Owner.getIdentityKey()`** (`model/Owner.java`) — now returns the 64-char lower-case hex SHA-256 over `normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName)` (via `Sha256Hex.lowerHex` and `Soundex.encode`), replacing the former plaintext `telephone|email|householdId`. The telephone and email are already normalized/lower-cased at the point this is computed in the create pipeline.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.isPossibleDuplicateOf(...)`** — the soft-match now triggers when the identity keys **differ** but **postcode** and **soundex(lastName)** match (previously: same postcode + case-insensitive lastName + different telephone). Added the `Soundex` import.

**Behavioural consequences that fall out of these two changes:**
- Two owners with the same lastName + postcode but **different telephones** now produce different identity keys → no 409; instead they're flagged as a soft match (same postcode + soundex, differing key).
- The identity key no longer contains `householdId`, so the single identity-key check is the only duplicate rule. The `householdId` is still computed and used for household size/membership-level capping. (There was no active household-duplicate 409 to remove — `HouseholdDuplicateException` was already never thrown.)
- The email-domain blocklist still runs first (in `normalizeOwnerFields`), and soft-deleted owners are still ignored (via `existingOwners()`) — both unchanged.

**Docs/comments** — updated the now-inaccurate Javadoc/comments in `Owner`, `OwnerRestControllerV1` (create pipeline, `rejectWhenIdentityInUse`, `applyHouseholdMembership`, `rejectDisallowedOwnerCreation`), and the `identityKey` / `possibleDuplicate` / `possibleDuplicateOf` descriptions and example in `openapi.yml`.

Both acceptance tests now pass: `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex` (asserts the returned key matches `[0-9a-f]{64}`) and `coreRejectsDuplicateIdentity` (identical telephone/email/lastName → 409).
